item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Tshisekedi personally established a consistent protective pattern. The available record instead shows recurring abuse, weak accountability, and severe prison and protest violence, with only scattered remedial actions.","evidence":[{"title":"2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo","publisher":"U.S. Department of State via ECOI","date":"2024","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128488.html","summary":"The report says the government made only limited progress on holding security-force abuses accountable, while credible reports included arbitrary killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary arrest or detention, and abuses by both security forces and armed groups. It also says some detention was incommunicado in unofficial facilities and that the government did not make efforts to prevent, investigate, or punish some disappearances.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-09-30","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/","summary":"Amnesty says Tshisekedi’s government failed to prevent and punish sexual violence and attacks against civilians, relied on a militarized state-of-siege approach, and allowed a crackdown on dissent through arbitrary detention and judicial harassment. It also says military courts had handed down more than a hundred death sentences after reinstatement of the death penalty.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-06-24","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/","summary":"Amnesty says the administration had made little progress on prior human-rights pledges, that security forces and affiliated militias continued to target civilians, and that the March 2024 death-penalty reinstatement was a serious rights regression. This is strong evidence against a protective record.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"DR Congo: Authorities must immediately free detained journalist","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-03-08","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/drc-authorities-must-immediately-free-detained-journalist/","summary":"Amnesty says the continued arbitrary detention of journalist Stanis Bujakera was judicial harassment meant to chill criticism, and it explicitly calls on Tshisekedi’s government to ensure release and media freedom. This is direct evidence of political imprisonment pressure rather than protection.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"DR Congo’s arrest of activists invokes déjà vu of growing repression","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-02-16","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/dr-congos-arrest-of-activists-invokes-deja-vu-of-growing-repression/","summary":"Amnesty says security services arrested LUCHA activists in a manner resembling abduction, kept some in unknown detention, and signaled a renewed crackdown on peaceful activists. This supports a finding that the state was not protecting residents from arbitrary detention or disappearance risks.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Democratic Republic of Congo","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo","summary":"HRW says government forces were involved in serious abuses, including killing dozens of civilians during enforcement of a protest ban in Goma, while repression against journalists, activists, critics, and peaceful protesters continued and opposition members were targeted.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"DR Congo: Investigate Prison Deaths, Sexual Violence","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-09-06","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/dr-congo-investigate-prison-deaths-sexual-violence","summary":"HRW says authorities should investigate the deadly Makala prison incident and provide a transparent account. This supports the conclusion that the state failed to protect detainees from violent abuse and mass harm in custody.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"More than 260 women sexually assaulted during Congo prison break, UN report shows","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-09-12","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/More-than-260-women-sexually-assaulted-during-Congo-prison-break-UN-reports-shows-47860482/","summary":"Reuters reports that at least 129 people were killed when prison guards used live fire during the Makala escape attempt and that more than 260 female inmates were sexually assaulted amid the chaos. This is some of the clearest evidence of state-inflicted lethal and sexual violence in custody.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"Congo lifts moratorium on death penalty, justice ministry circular shows","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-03-15","url":"https://www.yahoo.com/news/congo-lifts-moratorium-death-penalty-153836346.html","summary":"Reuters reports the government restored executions to rid the army of “traitors” and curb terrorism and banditry, with opponents warning the move opened the door to summary executions in a weak justice system. This is strong evidence of exemplary punishment rather than resident protection.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"Explainer-The foiled coup in DR Congo: Here’s what to know","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-05-20","url":"https://theprint.in/world/explainer-the-foiled-coup-in-dr-congo-heres-what-to-know/2093877/","summary":"Reuters reports armed men targeted top officials and briefly occupied the presidency complex before being stopped. This does not prove state abuse, but it shows the security environment remained volatile and coercive under Tshisekedi.","question_ids":["3B.1","2B.4"]},{"title":"Presidency / UN experts report reaction","publisher":"Présidence RDC","date":"2024-07-12","url":"https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_gouvernement_congolais_appelle_la_communaute_internationale_a_tirer_toutes_les_consequences_necessaires_du_nouveau_rapport_du_groupe_dexperts_des_nations_unies_sur_la_rdc","summary":"The presidency framed abuses as proof of Rwandan aggression and child recruitment by Rwanda-backed forces, which is more blame-shifting than internal accountability. This is relevant counterevidence because it shows limited acceptance of responsibility for abuses under Tshisekedi’s own control structure.","question_ids":["3B.1","2B.9"]},{"title":"2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo","publisher":"U.S. Department of State via ECOI","date":"2024","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128488.html","summary":"The report also notes the government took some steps to identify, investigate, prosecute, and punish officials who committed abuses. This is the main favorable evidence, but it is narrow and explicitly described as limited.","question_ids":["3B.1"]}]}
